subject.title: fix(security): bound plugin manifest reads in audit deep scan

question: Should deep audit reject installed plugin manifests above 1 MiB and continue with the existing warning plus plugin-directory scan without manifest-declared forced entries?
rationale: The implementation safely enforces the bound, but only the security owner can accept the chosen maximum and the remaining scan coverage for unusually large valid manifests.

options.title: Approve the 1 MiB boundary
options.body: Retain the current cap and visible warning because legitimate package manifests should remain well below the limit and the plugin root is still scanned.

options.title: Revise bounded coverage
options.body: Choose another cap or a bounded extraction strategy if unusually large manifests must retain forced scanning of declared entries.

recommendation.title: Approve the 1 MiB boundary
recommendation.body: Retain the current cap and visible warning because legitimate package manifests should remain well below the limit and the plugin root is still scanned.

likelyOwner.reason: This team is the explicit CODEOWNER for `src/security/` and therefore owns the audit threat-model decision.
